row: W2-R6 - the two bug fixes, on the device
setup: Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor running and recognised by the panel, Speed, character voice on (Ali G, heavy), knowledge base 2026.09.08

half_one_stray_computer_text.verdict: FAIL - the bug is not fixed
half_one_stray_computer_text.question_1: can you drop the tdp to save some battery
half_one_stray_computer_text.reply_1_tail: If you want to try dropping it down to a safer, lower setting, here's the block you need. Remember, this is just a suggestion, don't go too low or you'll be running hot!{"tdp_watts": 7, "gpu_clock_mhz": null}
half_one_stray_computer_text.question_2: what power limit should i use for this game
half_one_stray_computer_text.reply_2_tail: ...but don't go past that, yeah?{"tdp_watts": 13, "gpu_clock_mhz": null}
half_one_stray_computer_text.how_it_appears: Both replies end with the raw line inside a code box, rendered as <pre class="bonsai-md-fenced-pre"><code class="language-json">. Read from the page, not inferred.
half_one_stray_computer_text.root_cause: The plugin's own instruction tells the model to put the power block inside a fenced code block. The cleanup step that removes the block from what a person reads deliberately skips anything inside a fence, so that a code sample someone asked for is left alone. The one block the plugin asks for is therefore the one case the cleanup can never remove.
half_one_stray_computer_text.where: the fenced instruction is in ollama_prompts.py near line 1256; the fence exemption is in tdp_intent.py strip_tdp_recommendation_block
half_one_stray_computer_text.what_would_fix_it: Either stop asking for a fence and ask for a bare line, or teach the cleanup to remove a fenced block whose whole content is the power block and nothing else. The second is safer: it still leaves a real code example alone, because a real example is not exactly this one object.
half_one_stray_computer_text.note: The seven tests that shipped with the fix all pass. They test the unfenced case. Nothing tested the shape the plugin itself asks for.

half_two_line_names_a_closed_game.verdict: FAIL, with the cause now known
half_two_line_names_a_closed_game.seen: Exited the game through the Steam menu; RunningApps empty; the line under the question box still read 'Context: active game AppID 2321470' immediately after.
half_two_line_names_a_closed_game.new_evidence_this_session: The opposite failure was also measured. With the panel already open, the game was launched and the line said 'no active game detected' for 48 seconds and through a close and reopen of the Quick Access Menu, while Steam's own list had the game running the whole time. Restarting the plugin made the line correct at once, both times.
half_two_line_names_a_closed_game.root_cause: The panel reads which game is running once, when the plugin starts, and never again. That single fact explains both halves: a game that starts is never noticed, and a game that stops is never forgotten.
